# General Notes

- English uses strict positioning to identify different roles in a sentence
- In Arabic, the position of the words can change and the meaning will be maintained
    - The only way to know the role of a word in a sentence is through its status

# ![](data:image/png;base64,)Harakaat

There are 3 statuses:

- **Rafa**: Damma (generally is the doer) - Subject, default, doer
- **Nasb:** Fatha (generally is the object of the sentence) - Object
- **Jar:** Kasra (Harf Jar) - Prepositions, adverb

Nasb and Jar status are a response to something, Rafa is the something

# Dual

- **Rafa**: <ins>alif</ins> and noon انِ at the end
- **Nasb** and **Jarr**: y<ins>aa</ins> and noon يْنِ at the end
    - The letter before the Yaa ي (third-last letter) will always have a fatha  َ on it

# Plural

## **Masculine**

- **Rafa**: <ins>waw</ins> and noon ونِ at the end
- **Nasb** and **Jarr**: y<ins>aa</ins> and noon ينِ at the end

## Feminine

- Both have alif and ta ات at the end
    - **Rafa**: Ends with tanween dammah اتٌ
    - **Nasb** and **Jarr**: Ends with tanween kasrah اتٍ
